title: Electric clamping jaw based on bidirectional polarization type high-thrust electromagnet

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: Electric clamping jaw based on bidirectional polarization formula high thrust electro-magnet, including shell, electromagnetic drive mechanism, push rod, clamping jaw
features.note: The reference describes a shell (housing) containing an electromagnetic drive mechanism, which includes permanent magnets and an armature (displaceable magnet), and clamping jaws (workpiece contact surfaces).
features.refuted: Quote lists components but doesn't specify that the magnet is displaceable or describe pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.quote: armature 26 needs to drive the push rod 3 to move from back to front, then the push rod 3 drives the clamping jaw 4 to slide along the outer side of the shell 1
features.note: The armature (magnet) is described as moving to drive the push rod and clamping jaw, indicating displacement between positions.
features.refuted: Quote describes armature driving push rod and clamping jaw, not a magnet moving between gripping and release positions.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: clamping jaw 4 movable mounting is at the outside surface of limiting plate (5)
features.note: The reference describes 'clamping jaws' which act as workpiece contact surfaces, but it does not explicitly state they are 'pole shoes' or directly attached to the housing as such. They are mounted on a limiting plate.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: the front end permanent magnet 23 and the rear end permanent magnet 27 are respectively positioned on two sides of the soft magnet 25 with the same parameter and opposite magnetic poles.
features.note: The reference describes permanent magnets and a soft magnet within the electromagnetic drive, which inherently guide the magnetic field. However, it does not explicitly state that the 'clamping jaws' themselves are pole shoes designed to guide the magnetic field to the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not disclose any specific angle for the workpiece contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.note: The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet, but it does not specify the angle of the contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.

features.note: The reference explicitly states that the magnetic force keeps the clamping jaw (workpiece contact surface) with a certain clamping force on the workpiece.
features.refuted: Quote discusses magnetic induction line density after power failure but doesn't describe magnet pressing workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.quote: the outer shell (1) is cylindrical, and the installation shell (21) where the electromagnetic driving mechanism (2) is located is semi-cylindrical.
features.note: The housing is described as cylindrical, implying a longitudinal axis. The armature (magnet) moves 'from back to front', suggesting a displacement direction parallel to this axis. However, it is not explicitly stated that the displacement direction is parallel to the longitudinal axis of the cylindrical housing.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.quote: the front end permanent magnet 23 and the rear end permanent magnet 27 are respectively positioned on two sides of the soft magnet 25 with the same parameter and opposite magnetic poles.
features.note: The permanent magnets and soft magnet within the electromagnetic drive are part of directing the magnetic field. However, the 'clamping jaws' are not explicitly described as 'pole shoes' with active structures for directing the magnetic field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles on the workpiece contact surface or active structures.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.

features.note: The reference does not describe projections or recesses on the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any specific positioning device for the workpiece.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.quote: the front end permanent magnet 23 and the rear end permanent magnet 27 are respectively positioned on two sides of the soft magnet 25 with the same parameter and opposite magnetic poles.
features.note: The reference describes front and rear permanent magnets with opposite magnetic poles, which would create a north and south pole effect when activated.
features.refuted: Quote describes permanent magnets on two sides of soft magnet with opposite poles, not pole shoes acting as north and south poles in gripping position.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.

features.note: The reference describes the magnet (armature) being displaced by introducing direct current into a coil, indicating electrical displacement.
features.refuted: Quote describes current in coil generating magnetic induction lines, not displacement of magnet electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically.
